text.p: Australia have taken the anticipated decision to include replacement paceman Paul Reiffel in their team for the second test against England starting at Lord's on Thursday.
Reiffel was called up to join the touring party only last week because of injuries to fellow pace bowlers Jason Gillespie and Andy Bichel.
He had a six-wicket match haul in the Australians' 84-run victory over county champions Leicestershire in the three-day game that ended on Monday.
Reiffel's inclusion for Gillespie, who is shaking off a hamstring injury, is Australia's only change from the side beaten by nine wickets in the first test of the six-match series, at Edgbaston.
The Austalians have been heartened by Shane Warne's build-up to the Lord's test, following the leg-spinner's low-key performance at Edgbaston where his match return was one for 137.

Captain Mark Taylor said on the eve of the match on Wednesday: "Shane's a quality bowler and you don't lose it overnight. You never know with Warney, it might only take one ball and he'll be right back in it.
"I don't think injury is his problem. Reports that he has got to have an operation on his shoulder are not true. Just a bit of wear and tear, like we all have.

"It's just taking time to adjust over here to different conditions, a slight drop in form after five or six years, all those things take time to get used to. I think he's slowly improving all the time.
"He's certainly been looking good building up to this match. Like all of us he needs confidence and when he gets confidence he becomes a dangerous bowler."

Looking at his side's match prospects, Taylor said: "It's not a must win' situation, but it would be nice to win the game to square the series. We must make sure we don't give them a two days start like we did at Edgbaston."

England have opted not to play all-rounder Adam Hollioake -- he was released from their 13 on Tuesday so he could lead his county Surrey on Wednesday -- but they will wait until the morning of the test to decide on the final 11.
England skipper Michael Atherton said the pitch had felt a little damp, but gave no hint about whether fast bowler Devon Malcolm or left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell would be omitted.
He said: "We must approach this match in an attacking frame of mind. There are still five tests to go in this series, after all.
"But everyone is optimistic, and the mood around the country is upbeat. As a team we have felt that since Edgbaston, and we all appreciate those feelings."
